title: Meeting room booking requirements
idea: Scoping meeting room booking means naming who books rooms, what they do, the no-overlap rule for each room, and what v1 deliberately leaves out.
points: Employees find a free room, book it, check in, and cancel.
The core rule: two active bookings of one room never overlap.
A booking is a half-open interval, so back-to-back meetings both fit.
Assume one company, a few hundred rooms, and a busy Monday morning.

hero.title: Actors and use cases in v1

edges.caption: An employee starts with a time range and a headcount, and asks which rooms are free.
Some employees prefer to open one room's calendar and look for a gap.
Picking a room creates a Booking. The room is now blocked for that interval.
At the start time the organizer checks in, proving the room is really in use.
Cancelling before the meeting frees the interval for someone else.

edges.label: releases
edges.caption: The system is an actor: it releases bookings nobody checks in to within ten minutes.
Recurring series, external calendar sync and room admin screens wait for v2. Say so out loud.

code.title: Scope as an enum
code.caption: Use cases with their actor, the v1 cut as a range, and the overlap rule stated as code.

walk.text: v1 is a contiguous range of the enum, so the cut is one line.
Print each use case with its actor and an IN or OUT tag.
Test the core rule on a back-to-back pair and a real overlap.
Two intervals clash when each starts before the other ends.
Three actors: the employee, the facilities admin, and the system.
Admin screens, recurring series and calendar sync are listed, so the cut is visible.

pitfalls: Agree whether 11:00 end and 11:00 start clash before writing any overlap code.
Forgetting the no-show sweeper leaves rooms booked but empty all day.
State scale as an assumption; never present a guess as a measured number.

quiz.q: What does the first clash line of Scope print?
quiz.why: The intervals are half-open. 11:00 is not before 11:00, so the second check fails and back-to-back meetings do not clash.

takeaway: Fix the actors, the no-overlap rule and the v1 cut before any class.

starters: Should recurring meetings be in v1 for an interview answer?
How long should the no-show grace period be, and who decides?
What scale assumptions should I state for an office of this size?
